prompt:
The text below is drawn from an unprompted issue-salience survey, a measure of the priorities of the British electorate.

<source type="survey" instrument="Ipsos Issues Index" measurement="unprompted salience; multi-response" limitation="records salience only; direction not recoverable">
Issue salience, from a monthly national survey of British adults.

Question: what is the most important issue facing Britain, and what other issues are important? Unprompted, so respondents supply their own answers, and multi-response, so one person may name several. Percentages are the share of respondents mentioning each issue and therefore do not sum to 100. All 33 published categories are listed, in the survey's own wording.

  NHS/Hospitals/Healthcare                           41.0%
  Economy/Economic situation                         33.0%
  Immigration/Immigrants                             30.0%
  Inflation/Prices                                   29.0%
  Housing                                            17.0%
  Education/Schools                                  16.0%
  Defence/Foreign affairs/International terrorism    12.0%
  Poverty/Inequality                                 12.0%
  Lack of faith in politics/politicians/government   12.0%
  Other                                              11.0%
  Crime/Law and order/Violence/Vandalism             10.0%
  Pollution/Environment/Climate change                9.0%
  Taxation                                            7.0%
  Unemployment/Factory closure/Lack of industry       6.0%
  Transport/Public transport                          6.0%
  Ageing population/Social care                       6.0%
  Public services in general                          6.0%
  Common Market/Brexit/EU/Europe                      5.0%
  Low pay/Minimum wage/Fair wages                     5.0%
  Pensions/Social security/Benefits                   4.0%
  Local government/Council tax                        2.0%
  Race relations                                      2.0%
  Mental health/Well-being                            2.0%
  Coronavirus/Pandemic diseases                       2.0%
  Morality/Individual behaviour/Lifestyle             2.0%
  Food production/Farming                             1.0%
  Population levels/Overpopulation                    1.0%
  Nationalisation/Government control                  1.0%
  UK union/Devolution/Reform                          1.0%
  Nuclear weapons/Disarmament                         1.0%
  Drug abuse                                          1.0%
  Privatisation                                       1.0%
  Northern Ireland                                    1.0%

This instrument records that an issue was raised, not what respondents wanted done about it. It carries no measure of direction: nothing here indicates which way opinion leaned on any of these issues.
</source>

Your task is to construct a Moral Foundations profile for this electorate on the basis of the data above.

If the supplied data cannot support a judgment for a given foundation, return status "INSUFFICIENT" for that foundation and leave its weight null. Do not estimate. An INSUFFICIENT return is a correct answer, not a failure. Where a foundation is engaged but the data cannot resolve the direction of the appeal, return status "AMBIGUOUS".

Respond with a single JSON object and nothing else. Do not wrap it in markdown code fences and do not add commentary before or after it. The object must have exactly these keys, in this order:

{
  "justification": "<two sentences on how you read the data>",
  "foundations": [
    {"foundation": "care" | "loyalty" | "authority" | "sanctity" | "equality" | "proportionality",
     "basis": "<one line: which items in the data bear on this>",
     "status": "SCORED" | "AMBIGUOUS" | "INSUFFICIENT",
     "weight": <0-1> | null}
  ]
}

All six foundations must appear exactly once. The weights of entries with status "SCORED" must sum to 1. Entries with status "AMBIGUOUS" or "INSUFFICIENT" must have weight null.
